 Women’s Premier League side Delhi Capitals has appointed former Sri Lanka skipper Mahela Jayawardene as its Director of Cricket, the team announced on Friday.
 The 49-year-old takes up the role after recently stepping down as head coach of five-time Indian Premier League champion Mumbai Indians.
 Jayawardene will oversee all cricketing matters for the Capitals, including team strategy, talent identification, and player and coaching staff development.
 ALSO READ | Pat Cummins deserves benefit of the doubt, but his reputation should not exempt him from scrutiny 
 Speaking on his appointment, Jayawardene said, “Delhi Capitals has a strong identity and an exciting vision for the future of women’s cricket. I am delighted to take on the role of Director of Cricket for the WPL team.
 “The competition has enormous potential to shape the future of the women’s game, and I look forward to working with an established group of talented players and an experienced support team. My focus will be on building on the team’s existing strengths, bringing greater consistency to performances and ensuring we continue to evolve and compete for the title. I am excited about what we can achieve together,” he added.
